title: Bill and Account Collectors
description: Locate and notify customers of delinquent accounts by mail, telephone, or personal visit to solicit payment. Duties include receiving payment and posting amount to customer's account, preparing statements to credit department if customer fails to respond, initiating repossession proceedings or service disconnection, and keeping records of collection and status of accounts.

clusters.label: Communicating with People Outside the Organization

tasks.text: Locate and notify customers of delinquent accounts by mail, telephone, or personal visits to solicit payment.
Advise customers of necessary actions and strategies for debt repayment.
Confer with customers by telephone or in person to determine reasons for overdue payments and to review the terms of sales, service, or credit contracts.

clusters.label: Resolving Conflicts and Negotiating with Others

tasks.text: Arrange for debt repayment or establish repayment schedules, based on customers' financial situations.
Persuade customers to pay amounts due on credit accounts, damage claims, or nonpayable checks, or to return merchandise.
Record information about financial status of customers and status of collection efforts.
Perform various administrative functions for assigned accounts, such as recording address changes and purging the records of deceased customers.
Receive payments and post amounts paid to customer accounts.
Contact insurance companies to check on status of claims payments and write appeal letters for denial on claims.
Locate and monitor overdue accounts, using computers and a variety of automated systems.

clusters.label: Performing for or Working Directly with the Public

tasks.text: Answer customer questions regarding problems with their accounts.
Trace delinquent customers to new addresses by inquiring at post offices, telephone companies, credit bureaus, or through the questioning of neighbors.
Notify credit departments, order merchandise repossession or service disconnection, and turn over account records to attorneys when customers fail to respond to collection attempts.
Sort and file correspondence and perform miscellaneous clerical duties, such as answering correspondence and writing reports.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: Microsoft Dynamics GP, NetSuite ERP, SAP software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Accounting software
skills.def: Software to enable business functions relating to accounting, such as recording transactions or managing budgets. Examples: ADP Drive DMS for Accounting, Intuit QuickBooks, Oracle JD Edwards EnterpriseOne, Sage 50 Accounting.
